skill.name: framework-migration-legacy-modernize
skill.description: Guide incremental legacy system modernization through assessment, testing, strangler routing, security hardening, progressive rollout, decommissioning, and documentation.
skill.summary: Plan and validate gradual legacy system replacement while maintaining business continuity.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The sole static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a referenced file path. SKILL.md contains workflow instructions only, with no shell execution, executable code, prompt injection, or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 30 uses Markdown backticks to format a relative documentation path. It does not invoke Ruby, a shell, or any executable command.

content.value_statement: Legacy modernization can disrupt critical operations and hide integration risks. This skill structures assessment, testing, incremental replacement, rollout, and decommissioning with measurable safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Assesses technical debt, dependencies, business impact, and migration readiness.
Defines characterization, contract, performance, and test data coverage before changes.
Designs strangler routing, adapters, feature flags, fallbacks, and dual-system observability.
Organizes modernization waves by business value, technical risk, and quick-win potential.
Establishes progressive rollout gates, rollback triggers, and measurable success criteria.
Plans legacy decommissioning, documentation, and knowledge transfer after stable operation.
limitations: Provides workflow guidance and prompts; it does not independently inspect or modify a codebase.
Requires repository access, architecture context, business constraints, and production metrics for useful recommendations.
Suggested thresholds and technologies need adaptation to local service levels, regulations, and platform capabilities.
Does not replace security review, migration testing, or human approval for production changes.

use_cases.title: Build a modernization roadmap
use_cases.description: Prioritize legacy components using technical debt, dependencies, business criticality, risk, and quick-win potential.

use_cases.title: Establish migration safety tests
use_cases.description: Plan characterization, contract, performance, and data consistency testing before component replacement.

use_cases.title: Control a progressive rollout
use_cases.description: Define traffic stages, monitoring, automatic rollback triggers, fallback mechanisms, and observation periods.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a legacy system
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [system]. Identify technical debt, dependencies, business risks, quick wins, and missing information needed for modernization.

prompt_templates.title: Design migration test coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design testing for [components]. Include characterization tests, integration contracts, test data, performance baselines, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a strangler migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan migration for [component]. Define routing, adapters, data consistency, feature flags, observability, rollback triggers, and phased traffic percentages.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge an advanced migration plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [migration plan] against [constraints]. Rank failure modes, challenge assumptions, define automated gates, and specify evidence required for decommissioning.

output_examples.input: Assess a monolithic billing service for incremental modernization.
output_examples.output: Prioritize invoice rendering as a quick win, map database coupling, and add characterization tests before routing production traffic.

output_examples.input: Create a progressive rollout plan for a replacement API.
output_examples.output: Route traffic through 5%, 25%, 50%, and 100% stages. Roll back when errors exceed 1% or latency doubles.

output_examples.input: Define decommissioning criteria for a replaced component.
output_examples.output: Require 30 days at zero traffic, no remaining dependencies, archived documentation, updated pipelines, and approved data cleanup.

best_practices: Capture current behavior with characterization and contract tests before replacing components.
Define measurable rollback triggers and observe each rollout stage before increasing traffic.
Retain legacy fallbacks until dependency, traffic, data consistency, and stability evidence support decommissioning.
anti_patterns: Do not start implementation before mapping dependencies, business criticality, and shared data.
Do not use dual writes without reconciliation monitoring and a documented recovery process.
Do not decommission legacy components immediately after traffic reaches zero.

faq.question: What migration approach does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on gradual replacement through the strangler fig pattern, while also presenting feature, database, API, and full-cutover options.

faq.question: Can it perform a migration automatically?
faq.answer: No. It structures analysis and implementation work, but repository access, suitable tools, validation, and human approval remain necessary.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best results?
faq.answer: Provide the target codebase, architecture, dependencies, business criticality, service levels, compliance needs, current tests, and production metrics.

faq.question: Does it support full cutovers?
faq.answer: Yes. Full cutover is listed as an option, but it carries more risk than the default incremental approach.

faq.question: How does the workflow reduce migration risk?
faq.answer: It establishes tests, baselines, routing controls, monitoring, fallback mechanisms, progressive traffic stages, and explicit rollback triggers.

faq.question: When can a legacy component be decommissioned?
faq.answer: Decommission after 30 days at zero traffic, with dependencies removed, stability verified, documentation archived, and cleanup approved.
